newsitem.title: USA: Octagon former exec settles SEC charges.
newsitem.headline: Octagon former exec settles SEC charges.

text.p: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission said Thursday that Octagon Inc's former president and chief operating officer will pay $35,000 to settle charges he failed to disclose properly information about a contract and other transactions.

Without admitting or denying any wrong-doing, Steven Koinis settled the agency's charges he failed to disclose to shareholders accurate and timely information about private transactions with PRK Group, a company of which his wife was one-third owner, the SEC said.

PRK, an investment banking firm that was formed by the company's outside counsel, was paid a percentage of the total cost or value of any of Octagon's prospective mergers, acquisitions or other business combinations, the agency said.

Further, the agency said Koinis settled charges that he made "materially false and misleading disclosures about the magnitude of a major contract the company had entered into, which the company valued in news releases at $72.6 million.

In its administrative order, the SEC said Koinis approved public filings and news releases that contained the misleading information about the magnitude of that contract. Octagon shares nearly doubled during that time, the agency said.

"The commission is very concerned with the truthfulness and the timeliness of company disclosures and the Commission is very concerned that investors are fully informed about the transactions entered into by the company's officers," an SEC attorney said.
The agency has previously taken actions against the Reston, Va. environmental management company and another former officer.
Koinis' attorney could not be reached for comment.
